doc.title: Steve Turré interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 29, 2021

chapter: Rahsaan Roland Kirk and the conch shell
title: Ray Charles and first playing with Rahsaan Roland Kirk at 18
summary: Asked for an example of spirit, he names Ray Charles and Rahsaan, whom he first sat in with at 18 in San Francisco.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Okay. Was there a particular artist, you mentioned John Coltrane a little bit ago, and I wonder if there was a particular artist that you started listening to that was an on-spot example of what you’re talking about with the spirit, not just the technique and the instrumental prowess, but the spirit behind it?

I’ll give you a good example. My first big boss that took me around the world, Ray Charles, he had nothing but soul, nothing but soul there. No matter what he plays. He plays all kinds of music. A direct connection. Rahsaan Roland Kirk is another one. Rahsaan I first played with when I was 18 in San Francisco, before I left the Bay area, when he was in town I would play with him.
I’m wondering what was going through your head on the way home after that performance with Rahsaan Roland Kirk?
I was still hearing the music in my head after it was over. And I was excited as all get out and that reaffirmed to me that this is what I wanted to do.
Because I saw him when I was about 18 and I remember being completely overwhelmed with, I don’t have to tell you what — it’s like oh my God it’s like a force of nature.
He’s a spirit man, ain’t he?
Yeah Rahsaan is neat man, and boy could he play the blues, oh man. © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-
